experiments.name: Lawlor donor-held-out stimulation and marker recovery
experiments.design: Ten-fold leave-one-donor-out validation across baseline, LPS and anti-CD3/CD28 conditions
experiments.conclusion: The encoder change alone produced small, inconsistent differences. The donor-safe cross-modal readout recovered hidden markers substantially better than either native decoder, but totalVI-X and FusionVI-X were nearly tied. The useful signal came mainly from targeted cross-modal context.

experiments.name: Papalexi unseen CRISPR-target PD-L1 prediction
experiments.design: Five-fold leave-CRISPR-targets-out validation with 75 target-by-replicate effects
experiments.conclusion: FusionVI-X ranked unseen perturbation effects best and recovered expected IFNGR1, IFNGR2, JAK2 and STAT1 losses. It failed on CMTM6, a post-transcriptional PD-L1 stability mechanism, which defines a biologically meaningful limitation.

experiments.name: Original totalVI dataset targeted marker transfer
experiments.dataset: SLN111 mouse spleen and lymph-node CITE-seq
experiments.design: Two-fold leave-one-mouse-out validation with CD20, CD28, CD4 and CD8a masked together
experiments.conclusion: FusionVI modestly improved the native decoder, while the fixed cross-modal readouts were essentially tied. With only two mice this is a technical transfer result, not population-level evidence.

experiments.name: Paper-aligned full missing-protein-panel benchmark
experiments.dataset: SLN111 object used in totalVI Figure 3
experiments.design: SLN111-D1 retains RNA and proteins; the entire SLN111-D2 protein panel is hidden during training
experiments.conclusion: The missingness-aware FusionVI encoder reduced RMSLE by 0.57% and used 35% fewer parameters. Correlation metrics were slightly lower, so the supported claim is lower reconstruction error rather than universal superiority.
